Southeast Asia Haze Worsens, Triggering Mask Distribution and School Closures

Haze from intensifying Indonesian wildfires has worsened air quality across Southeast Asia, prompting Singapore to accelerate its distribution of N95 masks. In East Timor, schools were shut due to the pollution. Reporting from Singapore suggests a narrative framing the situation as an "act of God," with a lack of clarity on responsibility.
